title.narrative: Employment and decent work mainstreamed into national and sectoral development plans and programmes

description.narrative:
Zimbabwe has recorded periods of positive economic growth, driven mainly by agriculture, mining and services. However, job creation has lagged labour force growth, resulting in persistent youth unemployment, informality and precarious work especially for young people. In 2025, youths not-in employment, education and or training reached almost 50% (Q2 ZIMSTAT LFS). At the same time, ongoing labour market transformations-including the expansion of gig and platform-based work-are reshaping the nature, quality and security of employment. These dynamics highlight the urgency of aligning economic growth with employment outcomes, in line with the National Development Strategy 2 (NDS2), which prioritises job creation, formalisation, productivity and inclusive economic transformation.
A key milestone under this support will be the adoption and operationalisation of the National Employment Policy and the Formalisation Strategy. These frameworks strengthen national capacity to design and implement coherent, employment-centred policies that promote full and productive employment, enterprise development and sustainable job creation across priority sectors.
The ILO’s support emphasises policy advice, evidence generation and strengthened social dialogue mechanisms to embed employment outcomes at the centre of development planning. It seeks to promote increased decent job creation, through employment-intensive investments and sector value chain development; reduce informality, supported by policies and incentives to facilitate the transition of enterprises and workers to formality; enhance labour productivity and job quality, through skills development, lifelong learning and improved working conditions; expand access to labour market opportunities through targeted active labour market policies; and strengthen labour market governance, with improved data, evidence and institutional coordination for employment policy implementation.
